html:
Papua New Guinea is the eastern half of the island of New Guinea, with the Bismarck Archipelago and Bougainville. The map shows it from 1492 to 2010. Inland and in the highlands live Papuan peoples; many coasts and islands are home to Austronesian speakers descended from the Lapita. Its people speak more than 800 languages, more than any other country.

The colonial map was drawn in 1884. Germany took the northeast as German New Guinea, and Britain took the southeast, which passed to Australia in 1906 as the Territory of Papua. In the late 1800s labour recruiters, some little better than kidnappers, took islanders to plantations in Queensland and Samoa (blackbirding). Australia seized the German part in 1914 and ran it under a League of Nations mandate.

In the 1930s gold prospectors and patrol officers walked into the central highlands and found about a million people who had never met outsiders. In the Second World War Japan invaded in 1942, and Australian troops stopped its advance on Port Moresby in the Kokoda Track campaign.

The country became independent from Australia on 16 September 1975. A war on Bougainville over a huge copper mine lasted from 1988 to 1998.
